thread:
alice: Heads up — large spike in 5xx from hosted API right after the 12:07 deploy. Canary was set to 25% but traffic graphs show ~100% routed to canary in eu-west. https://dash.redwood/example :red_circle:
jamie: I see it, opening incident page. 502/504/timeouts from proxy layer; gateway logs show "upstream reset" and connection resets to canary pods.
devon: checking flag history and the rollout script now. looks like traffic-weight got set to 1.0 by a script.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started 2026-03-17T12:07Z (id: deploy-789). weight: 0.25 -> 1.0 (manual override detected).
maria: @devon can you confirm who did the override? ops shows a patch at 12:09 by jamie: `rbac.apply('traffic.weight', 1.0)` in ops/flags.
devon: confirmed — bug in the helper script: `SEED_WEIGHT=${WEIGHT:-1}` instead of `${WEIGHT:-0.25}`. that's why the default flipped. preparing rollback.
alice: repro quickly locally: `curl -s -D - https://api.redwood/v1/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" | head` returns HTTP/1.1 502 after ~2s consistently.
jamie: i pushed a hotfix because the canary was stuck and I thought we needed to shift weight to unblock seeding — didn't expect full flip. sorry. initiating rollback now. @oncall_tony can you help coordinate rollback so we avoid flapping?
oncall_tony: on it. applying patch to set traffic.weight=0.25 and pausing any auto-rollforward. patching now.
devon: looking at runtime logs — canary-serving pods show high latencies at seq len ~1024, and some OOM kills. the canary image enabled kernel-path=v2 and a larger batching window; might be a miscompiled kernel path causing memory blowups under production seqs. will pin to kernel-v1 after rollback.
maria: FYI CS is seeing elevated ticket volume and a couple of billing complaints (retries causing duplicate charge attempts). tagging billing-signal.
alice: adding customer-facing note to the status page and CS template.
jamie: rollback applied at 12:18Z, confirmed canary weight = 0.25. watching metrics.
sre-bot: metrics: 5xx rate in eu-west down ~60% after 2m, still elevated in na-west — route-tag mismatch still routing some NA traffic to eu canary. investigating route selector.
devon: short plan: 1) revert traffic flag (done) 2) demote kernel-v2 on canary build and build with kernel-v1 path 3) run canary at 10% for 10m with reduced batch window 4) run e2e load test before increasing weight. I'll open the PR with the guard.
oncall_tony: holding all rollouts for 2h and notifying squads. will update status page when we hit steady state.
maria: CS message drafted: "We're investigating increased 5xx errors following a recent rollout. We've rolled back to the prior configuration and are monitoring. Expected resolution 30-60 minutes; we'll update with more details." Posting now.
alice: quick debug commands I ran: 
```
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/canary -c runtime --since=15m | egrep "(upstream reset|timeout|OOM)"
curl -v https://api.redwood/health -H "x-region: eu-west"
```
jamie: sorry team. lesson learned: no manual override to traffic.weight without one SRE + 1 ops signoff. I’ll write a postmortem and follow up with the change to the helper script.
devon: opening PR now: add guard to helper script (disallow weight=1.0 without explicit --force), add e2e load test job in CI that runs a 2m seq-heavy workload, and pin canary image kernel path.
oncall_tony: status page updated at 12:28Z. metrics trending toward baseline. will keep channel open for 45m then close if stable.
sre-bot: incident note: rollback confirmed, partial routing leakage handled, no data leak detected. recommend blameless postmortem and an ops runbook update.
alice: thanks everyone — continuing to monitor.
sre-bot: incident closed at 13:10Z after 42m of monitoring. closing notes: follow-up PRs: #902 (helper guard), #903 (canary image pin), #904 (load test e2e).
